exclude: Runtime character buffer expanded from the four counted source streams at $AB1F–$BBD1.
extra: Shape cells in the VIC bank selected by the sprite pointer table.
The shared beginning of the round character set before the unpacker output.

comments.text: The processor port data direction register determines which bits of $01 control the CPU memory map.
The processor port selects the CPU memory map. In play $35 leaves I/O visible over $D000–$DFFF and maps RAM over BASIC and KERNAL.
Low byte of the horizontal camera position in pixel units. Round setup converts the word at $47 to cells by shifting it right three times.
High byte of the pixel position. Scroll and object code read the pair under interrupt masking where needed.
Low three bits supply the playfield's horizontal fine scroll at $0D6A. The footer interrupt clears those bits in the hardware register.
Gameplay sets this byte while requesting a character scroll. The playfield raster handler clears it after handling the shift.
The five keyboard tests rotate active-low results into this byte. AND with CIA1 port A merges the joystick state.
Zero-based round within an area. Round transitions advance it modulo four. The terrain, event and character-tail pointer tables use it.
One-hot area bit. Round wrap shifts it left. Object events use it as a mask to decide whether to instantiate a record.
The main-line delay at $0D39 consumes this flag and clears it after each wait.
The normal vitality-drain path stores $0B here when the high accumulator byte underflows.
Low byte of the vitality accumulator. Each normal drain subtracts $08 here and borrows from $74.
High byte of the vitality accumulator. The HUD groups four units into one full cell, with a cap of $60.
Set to $FF on a transition of combined control bit 4 from high to low.
Set to $FF on a transition of combined control bit 0 from high to low.
The screen shifter sets this flag after copying cells left. The raster handler takes the new-column path while it is set.
Vertical coordinate that feeds the player sprite position and terrain tests.
Status byte of the trailing player-associated record. The panel IRQ copies the player's status here before updating its position and pose.
Saves the combined control byte for comparing jump and fire bits on the following scan.
The patched F7 handler sets bit 7 while paused. The vitality update returns early while this bit is set.
In two-player switching, save $0660 here for player two and restore it when that player's turn resumes.
The initializer clears all 256 bytes on this page along with $0400–$06FF. Later code uses bytes near the end of the page as dispatch vectors.
Upper byte of the sprite-mask routine vector. The sprite-list adjustment routine copies it from the table at $C03E before dispatch.

Wait for raster line $10 and blank the display. Initialize screen memory, color RAM, the VIC bank, sprite mode and SID volume. Bank out KERNAL, install the RAM interrupt vectors, start the raster chain, then initialize game state.
Reset the area mask, set up the title state, request tune $15 and run the one- or two-player selection. Clear player score fields and initialize the first round on return.
Test the return-to-title flag and queue the previous update's sound. Deal with the completed-round flag before advancing the normal gameplay path.

Gameplay loop continuation. Update the music toggle on a key edge, redraw vitality and score, service terrain, objects, sprite lists and pause, then test the round outcome to select the continuation or life-handling path.
Inhibit vitality drain, blank the sprites and playfield, prepare the transition and advance the round modulo four. On wrap, shift the area bit and enter the area completion or final termination path.
Clear both bytes of camera X and fall through to the palette selector.
Select the packed tile color table and three background values by round index. Store the former in $69/$6A and the latter in $96, $0647 and $0648.
Four round-dependent values for the background register selected by the timed raster operand at $0D62.
Four round-dependent values copied to $0647 and installed by the playfield IRQ.
Four round-dependent values copied to $0648 and installed by the playfield IRQ.
Four pointers into the palette that follows each terrain stream. The pointed-to tables contain two color nybbles per byte.
Scan rows from the screen address $407E down column six. The first code outside the $90–$DF range after OR with $80 determines the starting Y as eight times the row index plus $22.
Wait for and clear the interrupt flag $6D one hundred times, then set $70 to $FF.

Acknowledge the raster interrupt, save registers, select the playfield character set and scroll, and install the next raster handler. With interrupts enabled again, decode a pending right column and run the requested character shift before restoring registers.
Immediate operand of LDY at $0D61. The helper at $3C07 rewrites it to select the playfield's first background color.
Clear fine scrolling for the panel and set $D018 to $0C. Restore the next playfield IRQ to $0D4B at raster line $4A, then enter the sprite work selected by $70 and $0632.
Immediate operand of LDA at $0E6F. The patched value is written to $D015 to mask the banner sprites on this path.
Drain vitality if $72 allows it, announce a new tick in $6D, service the sound driver, and tail-call the interrupt register restore.
The panel IRQ stores a flag here. The playfield IRQ checks it before performing the pending screen matrix copy.
Set the next IRQ to $0DE5 on line $FB, move all eight sprite Y registers to the patched value at $1121, and select eight more sprite pointers using $70 plus eight.
Copy eight consecutive pointer bytes from $C0C0 starting at X to the VIC screen's sprite pointer bytes at $43F8.
Load sprite 0 shape, color, X high mask, X expansion mask, X and Y from $04AD, $04E1, $0501, $0509, $04BD, $04CD. Continue down the register-write sequence.
Load sprite 1 shape, color, X high mask, X expansion mask, X and Y from $04AE, $04E2, $0502, $050A, $04BE, $04CE. Continue down the register-write sequence.
Load sprite 2 shape, color, X high mask, X expansion mask, X and Y from $04AF, $04E3, $0503, $050B, $04BF, $04CF. Continue down the register-write sequence.
Load sprite 3 shape, color, X high mask, X expansion mask, X and Y from $04B0, $04E4, $0504, $050C, $04C0, $04D0. Continue down the register-write sequence.
Load sprite 4 shape, color, X high mask, X expansion mask, X and Y from $04B1, $04E5, $0505, $050D, $04C1, $04D1. Continue down the register-write sequence.
Load sprite 5 shape, color, X high mask, X expansion mask, X and Y from $04B2, $04E6, $0506, $050E, $04C2, $04D2. Continue down the register-write sequence.
Load sprite 6 shape, color, X high mask, X expansion mask, X and Y from $04B3, $04E7, $0507, $050F, $04C3, $04D3. Continue down the register-write sequence.
Load sprite 7 shape, color, X high mask, X expansion mask, X and Y from $04B4, $04E8, $0508, $0510, $04C4, $04D4. Continue down the register-write sequence.
Compute the difference since the previous camera reading and apply it to the sprite list. On low-byte borrow, dispatch by sprite-list index through $C03E to toggle the prepared X masks.
Jump through the vector selected by the sprite index at $129D.
XOR bit mask $01 into $04D5 as the tracked sprite-list entry 0 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $02 into $04D5, $0501 as the tracked sprite-list entry 1 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $04 into $04D5, $0501, $0502 as the tracked sprite-list entry 2 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $08 into $04D5, $0501, $0502, $0503 as the tracked sprite-list entry 3 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $10 into $04D5, $0501, $0502, $0503, $0504 as the tracked sprite-list entry 4 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $20 into $04D5, $0501, $0502, $0503, $0504, $0505 as the tracked sprite-list entry 5 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $40 into $04D5, $0501, $0502, $0503, $0504, $0505, $0506 as the tracked sprite-list entry 6 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $80 into $04D5, $0501, $0502, $0503, $0504, $0505, $0506, $0507 as the tracked sprite-list entry 7 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $01 into $0501, $0502, $0503, $0504, $0505, $0506, $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 8 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $02 into $0502, $0503, $0504, $0505, $0506, $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 9 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $04 into $0503, $0504, $0505, $0506, $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 10 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $08 into $0504, $0505, $0506, $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 11 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $10 into $0505, $0506, $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 12 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $20 into $0506, $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 13 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $40 into $0507, $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 14 crosses the X boundary.
XOR bit mask $80 into $0508 as the tracked sprite-list entry 15 crosses the X boundary.
Wait briefly, then shift screen codes and color nybbles left by one cell using straight-line copies of the rows. Code from $150C through $1C84 performs the row copies with Y indexing.
Continuation of the screen and color RAM shift. This middle group continues the unrolled cell copies across the $42xx/$DAxx pages before passing to the $43xx/$DBxx group.

Walk 22 row records from $BC70. Each stores a stream pointer and a count, advanced by this routine as it emits the next rightmost screen code. Select a color nybble from the table at ($69) and write it to the corresponding color RAM cell.
Operand of AND at $1D32. The right-column routine changes it based on camera X before writing the emitted cell.
Initialize 22 row cursors from the selected length-prefixed streams and seed each repeat counter with $FF. Then look up the round's object event stream in $C300.

Select the round's compressed row data using $6B. Initialize 22 row cursors, skipping from the beginning of each row to the camera's starting cell for a nonzero position. Also seek the five-byte event stream to the restart threshold.
Four little-endian pointers to row streams at $8000, $9090, $9749 and $9CE7. Indexed by the zero-based round at $6B.

Initialize vitality and background, select round data, and decode the first right column. Build a visible starting field by requesting forty character shifts, then set the area and round digits and initialize per-attempt state.

Process five-byte event records before camera X plus $0140. Advance the cursor, require the event area mask to match $6C, and initialize an available actor. Read its type flags and call its initializer through the word table at $20CA.
Jump indirectly through the vector at $0780, set by the event spawner before its JSR here.
Choose $052A when the first slot's status is zero. Otherwise check twelve 16-byte slots from $056A for zero at offset $0C. On success, leave the record pointer in $57/$58 and return zero.
Clear offset $0C in each of the sixteen 16-byte actor records beginning at $052A.
Fill screen matrix bytes $4078 through $43FF with $A0, preserving the first three rows.
Set the active bit at offset $0C of the actor when its X coordinate is on the same page within $50 units to the right of the player.
Subtract player X from the actor X field pointed to by $57 and return the low byte in X and the high byte in A.
Word addresses for the spawn initializers. This portion starts with the shared $21EE initialization path.
The spawner reads the high byte of initializer addresses from this indexed base. The paired low byte is at $20CA.
Remaining dispatch words for object types $21 through $91, including the seven boss types $77–$7D that share $23F2.
Walk object records and call the type-specific conversion path for food types $61, $63, $65 and $67. Preserve the caller's actor pointer across the scan.

Initialise the boss timers and hit target from the area bit. Save the primary actor pointer in the actor records and create additional parts by copying the primary record and adjusting their positions and types.
One delay for each of seven areas. Boss initialization uses the lowest set area bit as its zero-based index and seeds both the reload and running timers.

Scan five keyboard controls with the CIA mask pairs at $2538. Combine their active-low results with the port 2 joystick from $DC00. Compare bits 4 and 0 to the previous poll and latch new fire and jump presses.
Five pairs traversed backwards by $24F3. The first byte selects columns on CIA1 port A and the second masks the reading from port B.
Select a keyboard column using the table at $BBF0 indexed by X and return the port B bits selected by the mask at $BC30.

Predict the player's next Y, clamp it to the field, and classify three cells beneath the player. Glyph codes after OR with $80 map to three classes divided at $90 and $E0. The returned base-three case routes the floor handling.
Convert the camera-relative X and prospective Y to a matrix position. Inspect a column of up to four cells and clear vertical motion on the obstructed path.

Compute the actor's camera-relative screen column and prospective collision row. Classify the three terrain cells into three ranges split at $90 and $E0. A position behind the camera uses a separate result path.
Multiply A by X with an eight-step shift-and-add loop, returning the unsigned product in $42/$43.
During downward motion, scan actor records with the active and platform flags. Test horizontal and vertical overlap, then place the player above a matching actor and reset vertical displacement.
Reject the test during an existing gameplay outcome. Compare actor and player coordinates to a finite horizontal distance and an asymmetric vertical window, returning $FF for overlap.
Test the two projectile slots at offsets $20 and $30. Require an active slot and overlapping X and Y, then return $FF for a collision or zero if neither passes.

Clear per-update jump and fire edges and advance the player pose counter. Every four phases replace eight bytes of a character shape staging table. A nonzero outcome selects the path that initializes and animates the loss state.
Return while the round flag is negative. When a boss round is finishing, check the player position and completion gate, then either use the normal control poll or a scripted rightward input.

Poll the joystick and keyboard, invert to active-high, choose horizontal and jump constants, and run object-platform and terrain handling. The terrain path ultimately dispatches by the surface code from $2551.
Read the middle terrain sample and choose one of fourteen height-profile entries based on camera-relative X phase. A code outside that range enters the common platform motion path.
Set the common motion constant to eight. Account for the jump edge and the current control-derived jump value before selecting the standing pose and movement branch.
Apply vertical motion to the player at actor offset zero, then to the attached platform object if $78 selects one.
Derive the rolling pose and target speed from the left control and motion state before applying movement. The routine keeps a nonzero speed when braking on this path.
Derive horizontal fractional state from the actor's velocity field. Use the signed vertical value to compute a candidate Y, with a cell-boundary correction when the collision branch requires it.
On a new fire press with the axe state set, use the first of two available projectile slots. Seed it from the player's position and facing, then request the throwing pose when movement state permits.
Fourteen vertical adjustments selected by the middle floor tile when bit 2 of camera-relative X is clear.
Fourteen vertical adjustments used when bit 2 of camera-relative X is set.

Advance the animation counter every fourth pass, scan the active actor records, and dispatch object updates through $35EA when their status permits. Actors that still await activation pass through $20A6.
Jump indirectly through the per-type handler vector at $0782.
The idle actor waits until it is within $5A units to the right of the player, then moves and switches phase at Y $9A. Axe contact enters the common hit handler with selector $29.
Test hits from either axe. On player contact copy the player's speed and facing into the egg actor, set its vertical motion and switch its type to $3A, the moving egg or contents path.

While the terrain case indicates a fall, adjust vertical motion and remove the actor if it drops past $E8. When placed on the terrain, restore the actor's intended type and run that type's initializer. Types $72 and $6B substitute $3D when the player lacks the axe.
Activate the motion state near the player. Advance falling motion when its terrain case is $0D and replace it with type $48 on the other terrain or hit path.

While the guardian state is negative, decrement the actor's timer and follow the player. At zero mark the departure phase. The departing path removes the actor after leaving the permitted vertical range.
Move the actor by one X unit, using status bit 3 for its direction. On reaching the camera or its stored bounds, flip the direction bit instead of committing a further step.
Choose between object types $23 and $24 from the terrain case. Drive its motion and count accepted axe contacts. The first changes the motion and the second enters hit handling with type $25.
Wait for the player to approach within $50 horizontal units, then update the actor until Y reaches $B5 and switch phase. The hit path uses effect type $30.

Subtract the actor's signed vertical velocity, compare the new Y against the stored limit for that direction and reverse on the bound. Advance horizontal motion and use the common hit routine on axe contact.
Scale the unsigned speed at actor offset 9 into a fixed-point delta. Add or subtract it from actor X and the fractional byte at offset $0F, according to the direction bit at offset $0C.
Run the axe overlap test. On contact, clear the colliding projectile's actor status, request sound 6 and return $FF.
Run the axe overlap test. On contact, set the projectile's direction bit, halve its horizontal speed, request sound $0A and return $FF.
146 little-endian update handlers, addressed by twice the actor type in $2DDB. Shared pointers route multiple types into the same update.
The actor update loop reads each handler's high address byte here at the same offset as its low byte at $35EA.
Remaining per-type update words beginning with type $21. Types $77–$7D share the main boss handler.

Collect actors with the relevant status bits and Y below $F0. Sort by Y when more than eight qualify, discard actors off the left edge, and prepare camera-relative positions and per-sprite flags for the raster handlers.
Map a sprite-list index modulo eight to a hardware register writer from $C01E and save the mask from $3933 alongside it.

Dispatch according to the boss phase. During the active fight, update side-to-side movement and its shot timer, count accepted axe hits and change the phase at the area-specific hit threshold. The defeated path moves a component downwards, then changes the boss actor into its post-fight state.
Use area-dependent pacing and bounce the boss between X $1050 and $10D0. Under the shot timer and hit flash tests, spawn type $84 and count a new hit only after the flash gate allows it.

Test for contact with a hit source when the boss hit cooldown is clear. Start a 12-tick flash and count the hit. At the end of the cooldown, compare the total to the area target and enter the defeated phase if reached.
Compute the part's rightward X offset and its vertical offset from the primary actor during the active phase. Branch to the special boss state path on phase zero and test axe deflection at the end.
Advance X right and Y up by two for a detached part until Y drops below $0A, then clear the actor. Area bit $40 selects the replacement type $34 instead.
Copy $97 and $96 into the live operands at $0D57 and $0D62, determining the VIC memory selection and first background value in a later IRQ.
Turn off play updates, seed music and background state and clear the top-left and vitality display fields. Continue into HUD setup.
Save A to $0653 and clear the patched operand at $0E70.
Seed $4B with $3F and return X equal to $15.
Run $1EC9 to prepare the round, then clear $72.
Disable all sprites and tail-call the 100-tick wait.
Blank the score cells and write two zero digits. For the second player path, clear its cells as well before updating the common cells and calling $0CBE.
Write A to the sprite X high-bit register and enable the display with raster compare bit 8 clear.
Disable sprites, set $70 to $20 for the banner, wait 100 ticks, and store the returned zero in the banner gate.
Test the F7 matrix bit, set $0661 while paused, and wait for release before accepting another press. The quit path sets $8F and clears $84 before leaving pause.
Use nested delay loops and poll the F7 matrix row until released. Restore X and Y from self-modified immediate operands.
Restore the JSR opcodes at $0DD0 and $0DD8, clear the playfield, and select the round character tail for the next playfield raster pass.
Save A as $0652, clear the current round and saved round fields, select the first area mask, initialize the HUD state, and open the banner gate.
VIC sprite shape selections for the screen at $4000. Both banner and actor rendering overwrite these bytes during raster processing.
VIC pointers $10 through $1F. Includes title animation cells starting at $10 and the second title sprite at $1F.
VIC pointers $20 through $2F. This group contains object silhouettes and repeats of terrain or obstacle shapes.
VIC pointers $30 through $3F. This group includes small creature and round object poses.
VIC pointers $40 through $4F. The contact sheet shows creature silhouettes and small collectible shapes.
VIC pointers $50 through $5F. This group contains thin projectiles and alternating walking creature poses.
VIC pointers $60 through $6F. Includes the player pose used by the bonus screen at pointer $6F.
VIC pointers $70 through $7F. A mixture of player poses, sprites with board-like silhouettes and bonus graphics.
VIC pointers $80 through $8F. The large display letters in this group include A through U with gaps.
VIC pointers $90 through $9F. The first cells include large banner digits followed by object shapes.
VIC pointers $A0 through $AF. Includes large creature silhouettes assembled from separate hardware cells.
VIC pointers $B0 through $BB. The contact sheet shows large shape fragments and cells with sparse pixel rows.
The prepare-round loop writes all 256 zero-page bytes here before the round starts.
Eight bytes per glyph. Screen codes below $80 include the vitality bar shapes, player and high-score logos, and the letters and numbers used by the title prompts.
Eight bytes per glyph for codes $80–$FF. These character cells include icon and pattern pieces used by the panel renderer.
First three glyphs in the round character set. The round-specific unpacker begins at the fourth glyph at $7818.

The mixed round color table. Each byte holds two color nybbles. The column decoder chooses the high nybble for even tile indices and the low nybble for odd indices.
Five byte values recognized by $F3D0. They mark zero, $FF, $AA, $55 and arbitrary-byte runs respectively.
One source pointer for each round. The unpacker begins writing at $7818 and stops at page $80.
First round's character-tail encoding, consuming $AB1F–$AF6F to produce the 253 glyphs after the first three shared entries.
Final compressed bytes of the forest glyph stream. The following run stream starts at $AF70.
Second round's character-tail encoding. This stream consumes $AF70–$B3A4 and expands to $7818–$7FFF.
Tail of the second glyph stream before the cave data at $B3A5.
Third round's character-tail encoding. This stream consumes $B3A5–$B7D0 and uses the same five run markers as the other rounds.
Tail of the third glyph stream before the mixed round's data at $B7D1.
Fourth round's character-tail encoding. This stream consumes $B7D1–$BBD1 and ends on the $8000 output boundary.
Indexed values written to CIA1 port A before the keyboard row read in $2542.
Values ANDed with CIA1 port B to return the selected keyboard bits to the caller.
Twenty-two three-byte row cursors built by $1DD8. Each contains a little-endian address and the remaining repeat state consumed by the right-column routine.
Four sprite pointers per type, addressed as $BCB2 plus four times the actor type plus the low two animation-phase bits at actor offset $0B.
Animation subtable overwritten with eight bytes by the player pose routine, using alternating ranges at $2DCB.
Subtable in the actor pointer store. The boss attack path rewrites four entries here at $3A58.
One byte per type, ORed into the starting status written to offset $0C by the object spawner.
Color per actor type, read when building the sprite list. Boss hit and recovery handlers overwrite the entry for the live boss type.
Eight pointers into the unrolled sprite register writer, with one entry per starting hardware slot.
High-byte operand base for the sprite reload pointers. The scheduler reads this and the preceding byte at the same index.
Two copies of masks $01 to $80. Render-list construction uses the first eight for the initial hardware sprite batch and the second eight for candidate replacements.
Sixteen code addresses selected by sprite-list index after an X-byte borrow. The handlers toggle the X flags in the affected sprite batches.
High-byte operand base paired with $C03E in the sprite mask dispatcher.
Little-endian screen matrix row addresses for collision tests. The callers convert a Y coordinate to an even offset into this table, then add the camera-relative column.
Dispatch for the base-three value produced by classifying three terrain cells under the player. The case is doubled before reading the handler address.
High byte of the first floor dispatch entry. The floor handler reads this base with the same index as $C08A.
Sprite shape pointer lists for the round and area banners. Round setup changes the two digit values before the banner is displayed.
Sprite pointer written by round initialization for the displayed round number.
Sprite pointer written by round initialization from the stage selector.
Eleven rows of thirty screen codes. $F473 copies these rows into the 40-column matrix before adding the remaining-vitality bonus.
Panel screen codes for player 1 and the high-score caption. Bit 7 ends the copy after the last caption glyph.
Panel screen codes beginning with player 2. Bit 7 on the last source byte terminates the copy.
First title string. The final byte $A1 both displays the exclamation mark and terminates the copy.
The F1 or F3 control legend. The final $B3 ends the string and displays digit 3.
The one- or two-player prompt. The high-bit final S ends the string.
Publisher and arcade copyright text beneath the title sprites. Ends at $C2CA with screen code $41 plus the terminator bit.
Seven groups of six bytes supplying three pairs of glyph-base and color values for the panel. The area mask determines the first group displayed.
Four little-endian event stream pointers. The zero-based round chooses $C30F, $C63B, $C8EF or $CB30.
Temporary first event built by $1EC9 during initial scrolling. Setup writes its X word before using it as the event cursor.
The $FFFF X threshold following the temporary setup event.
The first round's 162 five-byte object records, followed by $FFFF. Each record holds X as a little-endian word, Y, object type and an area mask in order.
The second round's 138 records. Their common five-byte format lets the event cursor skip records before the restart coordinate.
The third round's 115 records. The first record places type $61 at X $0098 and Y $8A in the areas selected by $2D.
The fourth round's 144 records, ending at the $FFFF X word at $CE00. The first two records share X $0098 and Y $8E with different object types and area masks.
Enter the sound request routine with the effect or tune selector in A.
Enter the sound tick routine at $E086.

Map the selector through $E06C to a request slot. Suppress a duplicate when the slot already holds that selector and is active. Otherwise store the selector and mark the slot pending, then restore X and Y.
Advance the sound counters and check the music-control byte before advancing the active voices.
Read the selector for request slot X, double it, and jump through the corresponding word at $E0EA.
Word table for selectors $00–$19. Zero routes to $E009. Selectors $15–$19 route to the five entry routines that initialize and tick score streams.
High address byte of the first sound dispatch entry. Indexed at the same offset as the low byte in $E0EA.
Initialize voice 3 with envelope $1F/$F9 and pulse width $707. The 16-step sequence uses $E169 for pitch high bytes and $E159 for changes to the control register.
Sixteen successive voice 3 control values. Zero entries preserve the register.
High-frequency offsets for sixteen steps of selector 1. The effect adds four to the indexed value.
Initialize voice 3 with envelope $0F/$F4 and pulse width $707, then use the 32-step countdown to select pitch and control bytes from $E1D6 and $E1B6.
Voice 3 control table, read with the inverted lower five timer bits. A zero skips the control write.
High pitch bytes for the 32-step selector 2. The low pitch byte is zero.
Use voice 3 with envelope $09/$F9 and pulse width $780. The later tick path writes a computed pitch high byte and zero low byte.
Start voice 3 with envelope $0F/$F8 and pulse width $707, then compute both frequency bytes and the waveform control for this slot.
Set voice 3 envelope to $0F/$FA and pulse width $707. The tick writes a zero frequency low byte and updates the high byte and waveform.
Selector 6, requested when an active axe hits an object at $35C8. The effect uses voice 3, envelope $0F/$F8 and pulse width $707.
Use voice 3 with envelope $0D/$FA. The tick also updates the high pulse width register in addition to the waveform and pitch.
Configure the third voice's envelope and pulse width to $0F/$F8 and $780, then write the sweep's frequency high byte and waveform.
Set up voice 3 with pulse width $780 and envelope $0F/$F8. The round bonus screen requests this selector before copying the text at $F473.
Selector $0A, requested by the deflection handler at $35E4. It uses envelope $0F/$FA and pulse width $780.
Set voice 3 envelope to $0F/$F9, use pulse width $780 and write a swept frequency with low byte zero.
Set voice 3 envelope $4F/$F9 and initial control $40. Count down from $40, transform the timer into a pitch high byte and use $E584 for waveform changes.
Sixteen control bytes selected by the quarter-speed timer index XOR $0F.
Configure envelope $0F/$F8 and pulse width $780. Clear filter routing and hold frequency at $0244 while the countdown indexes waveform bytes at $E5D5.
Control changes for selector $0D while the frequency word stays $0244.
The bonus loop requests this selector at $F5EF. Use voice 3 with envelope $0A/$F9 and clear filter routing before writing the timing-dependent pitch.
The dispatch slot for selector $0F immediately returns.

SID routine following the immediate RTS at the selector $0F entry. Its first-tick code configures voice 3 envelope $00/$F4 and pulse width $707, then writes pitch $0100 with waveform controlled by $E669.
Voice 3 waveform bytes following the selector $0F routine, indexed by the timer XOR one.
Configure envelope $0A/$FD on voice 3 and clear filter routing. Update voice 3 pitch high and control with frequency low kept at zero.
Use fixed voice 3 pitch high $27 and envelope $7A/$3E while changing the control byte according to the slot state.
Shared voice 3 effect. Count down from $20 and use the halved timer to select the waveform and pitch. The pitch index is reversed for selector $13.
Sixteen possible control values shared by selectors $12 and $13.
Voice 3 frequency high bytes, with reversed traversal for selector $13.
Set voice 3 frequency to $2000 and pulse width $707. Use envelope $0A/$F9, clear filter routing and run the waveform sequence.
Big-endian frequency lookup. The tune player adds the transposition offset to a score byte, then reads this base and the following base for the SID frequency pair.
Low-frequency-byte operand base paired with the high-frequency reference at $E7AD.
Jump to the stream command handler instead of trying to write the byte as a voice-1 pitch.

Count down a request slot. On expiry, read a three-voice pitch record unless the first byte selects a command. Values $C0 leave their voice untouched. For a pitch, add the transposition, load the frequency and toggle the gate before setting the next countdown.
Handle $C4 by writing all three stored waveforms back with the gate clear. Otherwise resolve the command through $E932 and tail-jump to its handler.
Music command table indexed by the opcode minus $C2. The $C4 case is handled before the indexed dispatch.
High byte of the command table's first entry. The dispatcher loads this table in parallel with the low byte preceding it.
Read attack/decay and sustain/release byte arguments, write them to voice 1 and advance to the next stream command.
Set both envelope registers for voice 2 from two stream arguments.
Set both envelope registers for voice 3 from two stream arguments.
Save the stream's one-byte waveform setting for later voice 1 gate changes.
Save the waveform byte written when a subsequent pitch starts on voice 2.
Copy the next stream byte to the saved control value for voice 3.
Write zero to attack/decay and sustain/release on all three voices and continue at the next command.
Restore the running slot's $FF start flag and return without reading another stream byte.
Save one stream argument as the countdown value reloaded after playing a pitch record.
Read the next two bytes as an absolute little-endian stream address, replace the cursor and dispatch there directly.
Save the current stream command address, then use the ordinary music jump code to go to the phrase.
Restore the single saved call position and advance past the three-byte phrase call.
Use the stream argument to select a frequency-table offset from $EA0C.
Write the next stream byte to SID register $D418 and continue.
Copy two music arguments to the low and high pulse width registers for voice 1.
Write the stream's two pulse width arguments to the second voice.
Write low and high pulse width bytes to the third voice.
Copy two stream bytes to the SID's cutoff registers.
Copy the next byte to $D417 and continue.
Write the cursor ahead by Y plus one, then jump back into the countdown path with A set to one to read the next event immediately.
On the first tick for this slot, point the music cursor to $EA9B and seed the countdown. When $FB is negative, the tick arrives only on one parity of the frame count.

The slot selected by $15 starts here with tempo, volume, envelope, waveform, pulse width and transposition commands. Subsequent records include notes and calls to local phrases. Selector $16 also uses shared phrases here.
Start this selector's cursor at $EC2E when its slot holds $FF. Apply the same $FB and frame-parity test as the $EA77 entry.
Tune stream entry for sound selector $16. It uses local and shared phrases, including a call into $EACF, and a return command at $ED9F.
Start with $EDBA and countdown one when this slot is new. Otherwise use the current countdown and stream pointer.
A compact tune for selector $17. The stream interpreter consumes all 79 bytes from here through the $C4 gate-off command at $EE08.
Initialize this stream slot to $EE23 or continue servicing its existing countdown.
First-tick path for selector $18. Set the cursor and prime the countdown.
The selector $18 stream initializes the driver, calls music phrase data through $EF2F and ends its main sequence with a gate-off command at $EE53.
Start this stream at $EF54 and use the extra-drain parity test before entering the common music tick.
Music selector $19 starts here. Its reachable pitch and command sequence extends through $EFE0 before the stream cursor repeats.
Copy a zero-based indexed string to the panel via $F230. Use only the low seven bits as the screen code and terminate after a source byte with bit 7 set.
Copy characters from the source pointer at $2A/$2B to the destination pointer at $24/$25. Bit 7 marks the last source byte and is stripped from the rendered character.
Color the player-name region and choose $C24A or $C260 by the player selector. Render the caption and refresh the three area badges.
Compare the current packed score to the stored high score and replace the high score when the subtraction has no borrow. Choose score sources for the panel from the selected player and play mode.
Draw three packed BCD bytes most significant first. Suppress initial zero digits and require the two units digits to be rendered.
Split the source byte into high and low nybbles. Convert them to digit screen codes, or to blanks while leading-zero suppression remains active.
Paint the meter's two color spans and render full and partial cells from $74. Divide into four vitality units per cell and index the partial cell shape table with the remainder.
Set the sixteen rightmost meter cells to yellow before choosing the visible fill glyphs.

Return while paused or when $FC is $18. Subtract $08 from the low vitality byte normally, or $14 on the extra-drain path selected by $FB. The ordinary path clamps an exhausted accumulator to zero and sets $6E to $0B. The extra-drain path sets $FB to $7F when the high byte falls below $0A.

Select a compressed stream through the round-indexed pointer table at $AB17 and expand it to $7818–$7FFF. Four markers at $AB12–$AB15 encode repeats of zero, $FF, $AA and $55. The fifth repeats an explicit value.

Request sound 9, copy eleven 30-column strings from $C100 to the playfield, set four color spans and show a sprite below the text. Then subtract from remaining vitality and add BCD points to the bonus total.
Advance the destination by 40 columns and loop for the next bonus row.

Subtract ten in decimal mode from the three-byte bonus. Add ten to the current score per iteration, redraw the remaining bonus and score, and play the count sound on borrow into the next byte. When the bonus underflows, clear its digits and stop.
Update the next score bytes in decimal mode. On a high-byte carry, handle the extra-life threshold at $03 and additional steps of $09 before exiting decimal mode.

Clear the field, select the panel character pages, write the four title strings, and enable the two sprites used in the title. The idle loop cycles one sprite picture and tests the one- and two-player matrix keys.
Fill the visible playfield's color RAM with the color argument in A, outside the top three rows.
Convert the one-hot area into a table index in steps of six and draw three badges in the panel, three screen columns apart.
Use a base glyph and its three successors for the two-by-two icon, and apply the entry's color to the same four cells.
While the round update is disabled, restore a fixed color across the captions. During play, cycle the highlighted player's eight caption colors when the pacing bits in $4B permit it.
